meta.title: Agentic AI Risk Assessment Workflow
meta.subtitle: A Multi-Agent n8n Pipeline for Banking Customer-Risk Screening

items.secondary: ISFA614 - Agentic AI Risk Assessment Workflow Orchestration

sidebar.title: Workflow Scale
captions: 8 CSV inputs: 5 data files + 3 rule files

paragraphs.text: This group lab builds an agentic AI workflow in n8n that assesses customer risk the way a bank's risk team might. Instead of asking one large model to do everything, the work is split across three specialist AI agents and one orchestrator agent.

An analyst uploads eight CSV files: five customer and transaction datasets, plus one rules file for each specialist. Each specialist evaluates every customer against its rules, the orchestrator consolidates their verdicts into one final decision per customer, and the workflow produces CSV reports and a management dashboard as an SVG.
A core design choice: risk policy lives in uploaded rule files rather than in the prompts, so rules can be added or changed without touching the workflow.

items.secondary: Evaluates customer profile data against the Agent-1 rules
Tests transfers and cash deposits against field / operator / value rules
Checks screening flags such as watchlist, sanctions, PEP and adverse media
Merges the three reports into a final decision per customer and a portfolio dashboard

tabsContent.title: Inputs and Outputs
tabsContent.description: One form submission in, five deliverables out:

items.secondary: F1 customer profile, F2 transactions, F3 transfers, F4 cash deposits, F5 regulatory screening, and the Agent-1, Agent-2 and Agent-3 rules files

sections.heading: Specialists apply rules, they don't decide policy
sections.body: Each specialist receives one customer record and its rule list, and must evaluate every rule exactly as written. The prompts explicitly forbid inventing, skipping or hard-coding rules, so adding a row to a rules CSV changes behaviour with no workflow edit.

sections.heading: A shared, structured answer
sections.body: All three specialists return the same seven fields (Customer_ID, Customer_Name, Risk_Level, Triggered_Rules, Supporting_Evidence, Summary, Recommended_Action), enforced by a Structured Output Parser, so their outputs can be merged and turned into CSV directly.

sections.heading: An orchestrator with a fixed hierarchy
sections.body: Agent-4 treats the specialist reports as the source of truth. Any HIGH makes the customer HIGH, otherwise any MEDIUM makes it MEDIUM, otherwise LOW, with fixed scores (90 / 60 / 20) and fixed actions (ESCALATE / MANUAL_REVIEW / APPROVE).

sections.heading: Code does the arithmetic
sections.body: The dashboard Code node recomputes totals, counts and percentages from the R4 array, so the headline numbers don't depend on the language model's calculations. The model contributes the narrative: the executive summary, red flags and recommendations.

items.title: Key Lesson: Keep a Human in the Loop

content.text: While troubleshooting, the team noticed output containing data that wasn't in the customer file. The cause was a misspelled field name, which meant Agent-4 received no data at all, and the model hallucinated its results instead of failing. It is a concrete example of why human review of agent output matters.

Splitting the work into specialised agents with clearly defined roles made the system more efficient and more robust than relying on a single AI for everything, and guardrails kept each agent inside its role.
